summary: Tue, 04 Aug 2026 01:40 - Added true stroked text outline to the live-subs overlay so captions stay legible on any background. Replaced the QGraphicsDropShadowEffect with a new OutlinedLabel(QLabel) that paints glyphs via QPainterPath: stroke pass with a round-join/round-cap pen of width 2*outline (so N px sits outside the glyph) then a fill pass. A drop shadow only offsets a blurred copy, so text still washes out against similarly-bright backgrounds; stroking every glyph edge is what burned-in subtitles do. Word wrapping is done in OutlinedLabel with QFontMetrics rather than by QLabel, because paintEvent and heightForWidth must agree on line count - if they disagreed the window would be sized for a different number of lines than it draws. Outline scales with font size (max(2, size/7)): 3px at 20pt, 6px at 40pt. Added --outline / -Outline (default 3, 0 disables) to the py script, Start-LiveSubtitles.ps1 and vw-commands.ps1. VERIFICATION NOTE: my first contrast test was invalid - it rendered the widget over a filled pixmap and got byte-identical pixel counts for white and black backgrounds, which proved the widget was painting its own background rather than compositing. Redone properly: render glyphs to a transparent pixmap, composite over each background, then count luminance extremes. Result over #FFFFFF/#000000/#7F7F7F/#F2C230/#2E6FF2 - ~1306 very-light glyph px and ~1900-2100 very-dark outline px present on every mid-tone, and counts now vary with background as they must. Re-ran the layout regression after swapping the label class: centre stable at cx=768, bottom stable at 735, grows upward 658->622, shrinks back 78->114->78, no clipping. Both ps1 parse clean.
